source.title: Grokking, Rank Minimization and Generalization in Deep Learning
source.authors: David Yunis; Kumar Kshitij Patel; Samuel Wheeler; P. Savarese; Gal Vardi; Karen Livescu; Michael Maire; Matthew R. Walter

record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on true and random CIFAR-10 labels and reports training error alongside rank dynamics, directly testing a part of V1 with a different analysis focus.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 random-label experiment reports zero training error for both random and true labels. Other results concern rank and generalization and do not test the listed claim versions. Values for the error curves appear only in Figure 8; the text states the outcome but provides no numeric error values.
record.test_reason: The zero-training-error results concern a four-layer MLP, whereas V1 specifies convolutional networks. The VGG experiments report training loss and spectral dynamics without an interpretable training classification error result in the supplied text. No own results test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 6: both label conditions reach zero training error but differ in rank and alignment. The broader conclusion is that generalization coincides with low-rank solutions in grokking, rank reduction also occurs across practical tasks, and weight decay promotes rank reduction; the authors do not establish a comprehensive causal theory.
record.recipe_differences: A 4-layer MLP on CIFAR-10, trained with constant-learning-rate SGD; the study measures spectral dynamics rather than comparing training recipes or model sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Label condition changes the observed rank and alignment dynamics: true-label training has lower middle-layer effective rank and persistent middle-layer alignment, whereas random-label alignment later disappears.

fits_no_version.finding: A four-layer MLP reaches zero training error on CIFAR-10 with either true or completely random labels after training with constant-rate momentum SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training can fit true and random CIFAR-10 labels to zero training error in a four-layer MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: Despite both label conditions reaching zero training error, true-label training produces lower middle-layer effective rank and more persistent inter-layer alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: True-label fitting and random-label memorization can differ in weight rank and alignment even when both achieve zero training error.

record.problems: Only 3 random seeds per experiment. The training-error results are described in text but their exact values are not tabulated; Figure 8 plots the curves. The experiment is a 4-layer MLP on CIFAR-10 and does not cover the broader size, architecture, optimizer, or dataset scope of V1.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. The VGG-16 CIFAR-10 experiment reports spectral dynamics and training losses but does not state a training classification error result relevant to the versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including random labels and the effects of size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and additional student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability training.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected states express inability to assess the specified claim versions, not doubt about the explicitly reported MLP zero-error outcomes. VGG training-loss findings are already declared in rows_left_out and do not supply readable near-zero classification error. Spectral alignment at initialization does not test V4's training-speed or trainable-depth claims.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, SGD or Adam comparisons, other convolutional networks, model size and early stopping sweeps, and regularized recipes.
